unique_sounds.banshee_scream: When a Parabolic Microphone or a Sound Recorder is used, the Banshee has a 33% chance of making 1 of its 20 unique screams instead of a regular paranormal sound.
unique_sounds.deogen_breath: If the player asks any question through the Spirit Box while standing within 1 metre of the Deogen, it has a 33% chance with each question to produce a unique response of constant heavy bull-like breathing, instead of a regular response.
unique_sounds.air_breath: The Oni cannot perform the mist form event, which involves a physical ball of fog moving towards the player, usually disappearing with a hiss sound upon collision.

hunts.fast_twin_los_top_speed: Fast twins top speed (Line Of Sight):

aswang.name: Aswang
aswang.description: Rumored to gorge itself on blood and corpses, the Aswang is feral yet capable of blending into urban environments.
aswang.hunt: Its line-of-sight acceleration increases its speed at a rate of 0.0375 times its base speed per second instead of 0.025, meaning it reaches its maximum speed after 17.33 seconds instead of 26 seconds for most other ghosts. The hunt will instantly end if the Aswang detects and reaches a player inside an available official hiding spot (such as a closet or a locker) used correctly, meaning it is impossible for players to be killed while hiding. However, if the Aswang were to end a hunt this way, then the next hunt will have a grace period of 0 seconds regardless of difficulty. Moreover, the ghost will have a 100% chance (instead of 50%) of remembering this place and returning to it unless it detects a player beforehand.

kormos.name: Kormos
kormos.description: Translating to the one who 'does not see', the Kormos is blind but uses its heightened hearing to hunt down victims.
kormos.hunt:
The Kormos has a hunt sanity threshold of 50% by default. It is increased to 70% if a player sprints in the same room as it.

During a hunt, the Kormos does not have visual line-of-sight and will therefore only detect players through voice chat and active electronic equipment. Due to having no line-of-sight, it cannot remember player locations between hunts and it will kill players by simply getting within 1.5 metres of them, ignoring obstacles such as furniture or walls.

The heightened hearing of the Kormos additionally allows it to sense players who are moving on the same floor, with specific ranges detailed in the following table:

| Player movement | 	Detection range |
| :--- | ---: |
| Walking while crouched | 	10 metres |
| Walking while standing | 	15 metres |
| Sprinting | 	30 metres |


If the pathing distance between the ghost and the player is strictly greater than 1.5 times the aforementioned ranges, the ghost ignores that player's movement.

The Monkey Paw's "I wish to be safe" wish will not make the Kormos able to sense player movement across the entire map.

All these cases place "detection waypoints", meaning that the ghost must first reach the waypoint before being able to travel to another waypoint. In addition to this, the Kormos verifies and places detection waypoints (if any) every 5-10 seconds and prioritizes in the following order:

- Sprinting
- Walking while standing
- Walking while crouched
- Voice/Electronics

In the case where multiple players are detected at the same time through the same movement type, the Kormos will prioritise the nearest waypoint.

When the Kormos detects a player through movement within 5 metres, it will enter a "pseudo-line-of-sight" phase and focus that player (overriding priority rules) by continuously updating its detection waypoint while also increasing its speed up to 1.65 times the base speed over 26 seconds.

Its current speed is multiplied by 1.3 if it travels to a detection waypoint that is further than 5 metres away.

banshee.name: Banshee
banshee.description: The singing siren, known for attracting its victims through song. It has been known to single out its prey before making a killing blow.
banshee.activity:
The Banshee has a higher chance of performing singing ghost events over other types.

If the hunt target is the target of a singing event and causes the Banshee to disappear prematurely (by going near it), then their sanity will decrease by 15%, instead of the usual 10%.

Like other ghosts, who the Banshee targets for a ghost event is random and based on distance; being the hunt target by itself does not increase their chance of being the ghost event target.

When in a D.O.T.S. state, the Banshee will try to move towards its hunt target instead of the nearest player.

Contrary to most other ghosts, the Banshee is able to perform long roams while its current room is not the favourite room.
banshee.ability:
When the Banshee performs a roam outside of hunts, if the hunt target is inside the investigation area, it has a 2/3 (67%) chance of triggering its ability which makes it travel to the target. Unlike the Wraith's and the Phantom's abilities, this will not create any EMF reading. The ability fails if the ghost and the hunt target are on different floors except if:
- The map is Point Hope
- The Banshee was in a single-room basement or a single-room attic for all other maps.
banshee.hunt:
At the start of the game a player is randomly selected as the hunt target. If the hunt target leaves the game or dies, a new hunt target will be selected. The new target is not random: the Banshee will select the first alive player in the list (established by the order the players joined the lobby) that is not the previous target, unless there is only one player remaining.

The Banshee's hunt threshold is 50%, but it only checks the target's sanity when trying to hunt, rather than the average sanity like other ghost types, meaning that only the target needs to be at or below 50% sanity for it to attempt to hunt. As a result, the Banshee can appear to start hunting from as high as 87% average sanity, or as low as 12% average sanity, on the Sanity Monitor, depending on the target's current sanity and number of other players.

When a Banshee hunts, it will mostly follow standard hunt rules, but it is unable to detect, and will ignore all players other than its hunt target. It will not attempt to chase other players and is unable to kill them, even if it comes into direct contact with a non-target player, instead passing through them. The Banshee will react to Incense lit by other players within range, but this will not allow for completion of the "Repel a ghost while it is chasing someone" optional objective unless the Banshee is also chasing its target when this occurs.

If the hunt target is outside the building, the Banshee will still use its target's sanity to decide whether to hunt. However, if it does hunt, it will hunt like any other ghost, chasing any opportune player.
banshee.misc: The Banshee can only be a female ghost and will use a female ghost model.

dayan.name: Dayan
dayan.description: The Dayan is born from the soul of someone who suffered immense cruelty in life. Now, in death, she is hyper-vigilant of anyone who 'dances' too close.
dayan.hunt: When a player is within 10 metres of the Dayan, whether on the same floor or not, the ghost will have a modified hunt sanity threshold and hunt speed. - If the closest player stay still, the threshold is decreased to 45% sanity. - If the closest player is walking, the threshold is increased to 65% sanity. If there is no player within 10 metres of the Dayan, it will have the standard threshold of 50% and follow standard ghost speeds with one particularity: if the Dayan has line-of-sight with a player within 10 metres, the speed increase from continuous line-of-sight adds in the background, and will only be applied once it is no longer near any player.
dayan.misc: The Dayan can only be a female ghost and will use a female ghost model.

demon.name: Demon
demon.description: A Demon is one of the worst ghosts you can encounter. It has been known to attack without reason.
demon.ability:
The Demon has an ability that allows it to automatically start a hunt, regardless of current average sanity. There is no particular behaviour or condition (such as requiring line-of-sight with a player) that affects if it activates or not; if it decides to use its ability, it will hunt. This hunt can be blocked by normal prevention methods.

Because the Demon's ability hunt is governed by the "ability phase", these hunts occur much less frequently than hunts derived from being below its sanity threshold. Additionally, as this is not a "proper" hunt attempt, the Demon can attempt to use its ability when it is unable to hunt (during the setup phase on Amateur and Intermediate difficulties, when it is affected by Incense, or when a hunt has just ended and it is on cooldown). However, it will fail and there will be no hunt.
demon.hunt:
The Demon has a normal hunt sanity threshold of 70%, instead of the standard 50%. This does not affect and is independent from its hunt ability, although the hunt does not differ in any way.

Demons have a minimum cooldown of 20 seconds between hunts, instead of the usual 25 seconds.

Smudging a Demon will prevent hunts for only 60 seconds, as opposed to the standard 90 seconds.

As a weakness, the effective range of a crucifix is 50% larger than the standard range:
- 4.5 metres instead of 3 for Tier I
- 6 metres instead of 4 for Tier II
- 7.5 metres instead of 5 for Tier III

deogen.name: Deogen
deogen.description:
Sometimes surrounded by an endless fog, Deogen have been eluding ghost hunters for years.
These ghosts have been reported to find even the most hidden prey, before stalking them into exhaustion.
deogen.hunt:
The Deogen's hunt sanity threshold is 40%, instead of the usual 50%.

During a hunt, the Deogen always has line-of-sight with all players on the map; in other words, it does not use the "roaming" mechanic. When the hunt begins, the Deogen will pick the nearest player (by straight-line distance) to move towards. It will focus that player for 10 seconds before being able to check and repick the nearest target every 5-10 seconds throughout the hunt. One can also use Incense to stun the Deogen temporarily and force it to change its target when the smudge effect runs out.

When the Deogen is chasing a player, its speed is based on its pathfinding distance to the target player and has three thresholds: above 6 meters, between 6 and 2.5 meters and below 2.5 meters.
- \> 6m: 3 m/s
- Between 2.5 - 6m: Assumed speed gradient between 0.4 - 3 m/s
- < 2.5m: 0.4 m/s

If the Deogen is smudged or is otherwise not chasing any player, its speed will remain at its current speed, or 1.6 m/s if its current speed is greater than 3 m/s. Otherwise, the Deogen does not alter its speed based on line-of-sight while chasing a player.

During a hunt, the Deogen flickers and is on average invisible for shorter and visible for longer compared to most other ghosts.

|Ghost |	Visibility length (s) | Invisibility length (s) | Total per-flicker length (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
|Deogen |	0.20 - 0.30 |	0.01 - 0.40 |	0.30 - 0.60 |
|Standard ghost |	0.08 - 0.30 |	0.10 - 0.92 |	0.30 - 1.00 |

gallu.name: Gallu
gallu.description: Another form of demon, the Gallu is a reminder that death comes for us all. Using protective equipment provokes the ghost until it's no longer effective.
gallu.activity: The Gallu cannot disturb salt piles while in its enraged state.
gallu.ability:
The Gallu has three states it can switch to: "normal", "enraged", and "weakened". By default, it starts in the normal state, where it behaves like a standard ghost. It will change from the normal state to the enraged state or from the weakened state to the normal state:
- instantly after burning a crucifix
- instantly after the end of the incense's blinding effect during a hunt
- after a duration equal to the last blinding effect from an incense after being affected by incense outside of a hunt
	- instantly if no incense were used during any previous hunts
	- 4 seconds if the Gallu was last blinded while in an enraged state
	- 5 seconds if the Gallu was last blinded while in a normal state
	- 6 seconds if the Gallu was last blinded while in a weakened state
- 2 seconds after stepping in salt if its current state is "normal"
- 3 seconds after stepping in salt if its current state is "weakened"

The state changes cannot be queued. For example, a weakened Gallu stepping in a second salt pile 1 second after stepping into the first one will not make it change into the enraged state 1 second after changing into the normal state.
gallu.hunt:
If a hunt ends while the Gallu is in its enraged state, it will instantly switch to the weakened state.

|Behavior |	Normal state |	Enraged state |	Weakened state |
|---|---|---|---|
|Hunt sanity threshold |	50% |	60% |	40% |
|Crucifix range |	Standard |	-2 meters |	+1 meter |
|Hunt base speed |	1.7 m/s |	1.955 m/s |	1.36 m/s |
|Incense's blinding effect |	5 seconds |	4 seconds |	6 seconds |

goryo.name: Goryo
goryo.description: When a Goryo passes through a DOTS projector, using a video camera is the only way to see it.
goryo.activity:
When performing a roam, the Goryo can only perform short roams, rather than either short or long roams.

The Goryo will not roam away from its favorite room as often as other ghosts and cannot change its favorite room in any difficulty. This can only be overridden via the "sanity wish" when using the Monkey Paw.

The Goryo will only enter in a D.O.T.S state if no players are in the same room as the ghost. In addition, its D.O.T.S silhouette is only visible through a Video Camera, and cannot be seen with the naked eye. A Goryo will still manifest normally during ghost events and hunts.

The Goryo will enter the D.O.T.S state more frequently than other ghosts.

hantu.name: Hantu
hantu.description: A Hantu is a rare ghost that thrives in the coldest climates. The cold seems to make them more aggressive and empowered.
hantu.activity: The Hantu cannot turn on the fuse box, and is twice as likely to turn it off.
hantu.hunt:
During a hunt, the Hantu's speed is affected by the temperature of the room that it goes through.

|Room temperature |	Ghost speed (m/s) |
|:---:|:---:|
|> 15°C (59°F) |	1.4 |
|12–15°C (53.6–59°F) |	1.75 |
|9–12°C (48.2–53.6°F) |	2.1 |
|6–9°C (42.8–48.2°F) |	2.3 |
|3–6°C (37.4–42.8°F) |	2.4 |
|0–3°C (32–37.4°F) |	2.5 |
|< 0°C (32°F) |	2.7 |

Unlike most other ghosts, the Hantu does not have line-of-sight acceleration during hunts.

During a hunt, the Hantu will emit freezing breath near its head in any room as long as the fuse box is off. Dead players cannot see this breath. As this is not actual "evidence", it can appear on any difficulty.

jinn.name: Jinn
jinn.description: A Jinn is a territorial ghost that will attack when threatened. It has also been known to be able to travel at significant speed.
jinn.activity: The Jinn cannot directly turn off the fuse box. However, it can still indirectly turn off the fuse box by turning too many lights on and overloading it.
jinn.ability: When near a player and the fuse box is on, the Jinn will occasionally use an ability that lowers the sanity of one player in the same room or otherwise within 3 meters of it by 25%. The player who will lose sanity is the first in the list (established by the order the players joined the lobby) among players in range. An EMF 2 or 5 reading will then be generated at the fuse box.
jinn.hunt: During a hunt, if all of the following three criteria are satisfied: - The fuse box is turned on The Jinn has line-of-sight with a player it is targeting The Jinn is further than 3 metres from that player Then its speed will be fixed while the criteria are met. Otherwise, it will obey standard ghost speeds with one particularity: while it is travelling at the fixed speed, the speed increase from continuous line-of-sight adds in the background, and will be applied once one criteria is no longer satisfied.

mare.name: Mare
mare.description: A Mare is the source of all nightmares, making it most powerful in the dark.
mare.activity:
Mares cannot interact with lights to turn them on, and they are more likely to choose turning off lights as an interaction. They also cannot perform the light flickering interaction (the one that specifically leaves an EMF reading at a light switch as opposed to the "atmospheric" light flickering).

The Mare does not have any affinity with computer monitors, televisions, Bleasdale Farmhouse's motion activated lights, and the fuse box, and can turn them on or off like most other ghosts. The Mare also does not have any affinity with fire sources and can still light them up.

The Mare has a higher chance of performing light-shattering ghost events over other types, as this will disable the lights, making it easier to hunt.

When the lights are on in its current room, the Mare is more likely to perform long roams.

Contrary to most other ghosts, the Mare is able to perform long roams while its current room is not the favourite room.
mare.ability: If a player turns on a light (excluding TVs and computers) that is within 4 metres of a Mare, it has a 1/7 chance of turning the light off almost instantly, with a maximum delay of 1 second. Each light has a cooldown per player of 10 seconds after it has been turned on or off, and the Mare cannot perform its ability on a light that has an active cooldown. The Mare can use this ability even if the fuse box is turned off or broken, but not if the light is shattered. The ability also works during a ghost event.
mare.hunt: A Mare has a modified hunt sanity threshold depending on whether the room it is currently in is lit. If the lights are turned off, the hunt sanity threshold is increased to 60%, and if the lights are turned on, the threshold is decreased to 40%. This applies even if the fuse box is turned off or broken, but not if the room's lights are destroyed. Other sources of light, such as brought-in equipment and Firelights, do not affect this threshold.

moroi.name: Moroi
moroi.description: Moroi have risen from the grave to drain energy from the living. They have been known to place curses on their victims, curable only by antidotes or moving very far away.
moroi.ability:
The Moroi has an ability to "curse" a target through the following ways:
- By successfully obtaining a response from the Spirit Box; this will curse the person who "caused" the response, either by asking questions or triggering the failsafe.
- By hearing paranormal sounds through the Parabolic Microphone.
- By successfully recording any sound with the Sound Recorder.

When a player is cursed, their passive sanity drain is doubled and being in a lit area will no longer prevent sanity drain (i.e. the player is considered in the dark at all times). Leaving the investigation area will still pause the sanity drain, and firelights will still mitigate the sanity drain. Consuming Sanity Medication removes the curse for that player. Players that have been cursed before in the contract can be cursed again. Multiple players can be cursed at the same time, but curses do not stack on a single player.
moroi.hunt:
The Moroi's speed is dependent on the average sanity, and will change during a hunt according to the current average sanity.

|Average sanity % |	Base ghost speed |
|:---:|:---:|
|≥ 45%|	1.5 m/s |
|40% - 45%|	1.583 m/s |
|35% - 40%|	1.66 m/s |
|30% - 35%|	1.749 m/s |
|25% - 30%|	1.832 m/s |
|20% - 25%|	1.915 m/s |
|15% - 20%|	1.998 m/s |
|10% - 15%|	2.081 m/s |
|5% - 10%|	2.164 m/s |
|0% - 5%|	2.25 m/s |

When using an Incense during a hunt, the duration where the Moroi cannot see nor kill players is 7.5 seconds instead of 5.

myling.name: Myling
myling.description: A Myling is a very vocal and active ghost. They are rumoured to be quiet when hunting their prey.
myling.activity: The Myling produces a paranormal sound (groaning/laughing/talking/whisper) on a Parabolic Microphone or a Sound Recorder every 64 - 127 seconds, instead of every 80 - 127 seconds for other ghosts.
myling.hunt: When hunting, a Myling's footstep and vocalization sounds will only be audible to players within 12 meters – slightly greater than the range required for electronic interference – instead of the usual 20 meters. The volume of footsteps is slightly muffled near the limit, but quickly becomes discernible as it approaches.

obake.name: Obake
obake.description: Obake are terrifying shape-shifters, capable of taking on many forms. They have been seen taking on humanoid shapes to attract their prey.
obake.activity: Each time the Obake interacts with a valid surface, it has a 75% chance of leaving fingerprints, instead of the usual 100%. After stepping in salt, it also has a 75% chance each step, instead of 100%, of leaving a footprint, creating no footstep sound when the chance fails. In multiplayer, the missing footprints are not synchronized between players, which may lead to a different number of footprints and footstep sounds for each player. When creating handprints or fingerprints, there is a one-sixth (~16.7%) chance for the Obake to create a unique handprint/fingerprint pattern: - A six-fingered handprint instead of the usual five fingers - Two fingerprints instead of one on light switches, lamps, and TV remotes - Five fingerprints instead of four on keyboards and Prison cell doors When performing a fake hunt ghost event or a Music Box event, the Obake is the only ghost that will sometimes miss a footstep sound. This is very likely a bug.
obake.ability: The Obake occasionally triggers an ability to reduce the remaining time for all existing fingerprints on the map by half. For example, two fingerprints lingering on the map with 40 seconds and 70 seconds before timing out and disappearing are cut in half to 20 and 35 seconds remaining respectively. This ability can be triggered multiple times in quick succession, making it possible for an instance of fingerprints to last for mere seconds before vanishing.
obake.hunt: During a hunt, the Obake will occasionally shapeshift into a different ghost model of the same gender during a flicker. Dead players cannot see this shapeshift. A shapeshift will always occur on the 12th, 27th, 39th, 54th, 62nd, 80th, 105th, 120th, and 132nd flickers (starting with the first flicker-in) of a hunt. - This means that the first shapeshift will happen approximately 7 - 9 seconds after the grace period ends. - This also means that the Obake will not shapeshift at all if the hunt ends prematurely (after the ghost kills a player or when all players leave the investigation area), as it will not have the time to reach the 12th flicker. When shapeshifting, the Obake has an order of models it will use. The first shapeshift of the contract will always be using the first ghost model in the following list. The second shapeshift will then use the second model, the third one the third model, and so on with the list looping on itself. When the Obake reaches its own model in the list, it will shapeshift into itself with a more or less visible posture reset. |Male ghosts|Female ghosts| |---|---| |→→→→→→| →→→ | Both the shapeshifting and the fingerprint duration's reduction will count as an ability in the post-game statistics.

obambo.name: Obambo
obambo.description: The Obambo is the ghost of someone never properly laid to rest. Fickle and defensive, it flickers between states of calm and aggression.
obambo.activity:
The Obambo has two states: "calm" and "aggressive". It always starts in the calm state at the beginning of a contract before switching to the other state 1 minute after an exit door is opened for the first time, then every 2 minutes. The state switch can happen during a hunt.

Depending on its state, the Obambo will either have very high activity or low activity, respectively when calm and aggressive.
obambo.hunt:
The Obambo has a hunt sanity threshold of 10% while in its calm state, and of 65% in its aggressive state.

The Obambo speed depends on it's current state.

The hunt duration will be 20% shorter if the Obambo starts the hunt in the aggressive state. This will apply even if the ghost switches to the calm state mid-hunt. You should expect your hunt to last {{huntDuration}} seconds.

oni.name: Oni
oni.description: Onis love to scare their victims as much as possible before attacking. They are often seen in their physical form, guarding their place of death.
oni.activity:
The Oni is more active, interacting with objects more often, when there is at least one player in the same room as it.

When performing a ghost event, the Oni:
- Cannot perform the mist form event.
- Will prefer showing in its full form during a manifestation event as opposed to a shadowy or translucent form.
- Will have double the sanity drain of other ghosts when colliding with the target player in a ghost event (so 20% instead of 10%).
oni.hunt:
During a hunt, the Oni flickers and is on average invisible for shorter and visible for longer compared to most other ghosts.

|Ghost |	Visibility length (s) |	Invisibility length (s) |	Total per-flicker length (s)|
|---|---|---|---|
|Oni |	0.02 - 0.50 |	0.01 - 0.50 |	0.30 - 1.00|
|Standard ghost |	0.08 - 0.30 |	0.10 - 0.92 |	0.30 - 1.00|

onryo.name: Onryo
onryo.description: The Onryo is often referred to as "The Wrathful Spirit". It steals souls from dying victims' bodies to seek revenge. This ghost has been known to fear any form of fire, and will do anything to be far from it.
onryo.activity:
The Onryo cannot light any fire sources (fireplaces, campfires, and candles) naturally, but can be forced into doing so with a Voodoo Doll.

The Onryo's flame blowing frequency increases the more dead players there are:

|Number of dead players |	Chance of blowing out the flame |	Chance of blowing out the tier II firelight	| Cooldown before the Onryo can attempt to blow out the flame after lighting (not first lighting)|
|---|---|---|---|
|0|	66.67% |	96.3% |	20 - 80 seconds|
|1|	75% |	98.43% |	20 - 60 seconds|
|2|	80% |	99.2% |	20 - 40 seconds|
|3|	83.33% |	99.54% |	20 seconds|

The cooldown before the Onryo can attempt to blow out the flame after lighting does not concern the first lighting.
onryo.ability:
The Onryo checks a counter of flame blowouts each time it exits the idle state. If the counter is greater than or equal to 3, and provided there is currently no hunt cooldown and no incense's cleansing effect, the Onryo will use its ability, which resets the blowout counter to 0 before initiating a hunt regardless of current average sanity. This hunt can be blocked by the setup phase still being active, a crucifix, or another flame.
- A flame preventing a hunt or blown out during a hunt will still increase the counter by 1.
- If the counter reaches 3 during a hunt or an incense's cleansing effect, it will instantly reset to 0 and cancel the Onryo's ability.
onryo.hunt:
The Onryo has a hunt sanity threshold of 60% by default. When it is near a flame, this threshold is decreased to 40%.

If the Onryo attempts a hunt within 4 metres of any type of flame (e.g. firelight, igniter, campfire, etc.), it will blow out the flame instead, and the hunt will fail. This does not restart the hunt cooldown timer, unlike a crucifix. If both a crucifix and a flame are within range, the flame will take priority over the crucifix for preventing the hunt.
- The Onryo's hunt attempts also override a flame's individual cooldowns, making it capable of blowing out a firelight within 30 seconds of its first lighting, or within 20 seconds of its subsequent lightings. Note that a tier III firelight's current cooldown is paused if it is turned off by the player or an Onryo's hunt attempt.

phantom.name: Phantom
phantom.description: A Phantom is a ghost that can possess the living, inducing fear into those around it. They are most commonly summoned from Ouija Boards.
phantom.activity:
When capturing a photo/video of a Phantom, whether it be in its full form, translucent form, shadow form, or D.O.T.S state, the ghost will physically disappear (but remain in its previous state, e.g. a ghost event) once the capture is successful, and the resulting media will contain no visible ghost and no interference.
- If the photo/video was taken during a ghost event, electronic equipment will also cease to malfunction and the player's heartbeats will stop playing.
- If the photo/video was taken during a hunt, the ghost will briefly disappear before continuing to physically flash in and out.

Being within 10 metres of a Phantom while in pseudo line-of-sight (where heartbeats play) reduces the player's sanity by 0.5%/s. This only applies during ghost events and hunts, and is separate from passive sanity drain. This does not apply during ghost events if the Phantom was made invisible by taking a picture.
phantom.ability: The Phantom has an ability where it will choose a random player and travel to a spot within 5 metres of their location (as opposed to a regular roam). This will create an EMF Level 2 reading at the location where the roam ended, at the level of the targeted player's head when uncrouched. This behavior is somewhat similar to that of the Banshee and the Wraith; unlike Banshees, Phantoms do not select a player to target until they die or leave the game, and do not do this as often; and unlike Wraiths, the Phantom physically walks to that point rather than teleporting, and will set off Motion Sensors and disturb Salt on the way to it.
phantom.hunt:
During a hunt, the Phantom flickers and is on average visible for shorter and invisible for longer compared to most other ghosts.

|Ghost|	Visibility length (s)|	Invisibility length (s)|	Total per-flicker length (s)|
|---|---|---|---|
|Phantom|	0.08 - 0.30|	0.70 - 1.92|	1.00 - 2.00|
|Standard ghost|	0.08 - 0.30|	0.10 - 0.92|	0.30 - 1.00|

poltergeist.name: Poltergeist
poltergeist.description: One of the most famous ghosts, the Poltergeist. Known to manipulate objects around it to spread fear into its victims.
poltergeist.activity:
In general, the Poltergeist is more likely to throw items.

The Poltergeist's throwing power is of 2 - 6 horizontally and 3 - 6 vertically, while it respectively of 1 - 3 and 1 - 5 for other ghosts.
poltergeist.ability: The Poltergeist will occasionally use an ability that allows it to throw multiple nearby items at once, creating an EMF level 2 reading (the thrown items themselves generate EMF 3). This will decrease the sanity of all nearby players in line-of-sight with the EMF 2 location by 2% per item thrown. The Poltergeist can use this ability even while the lights in its current room are on. If there are no items near a Poltergeist, it is unable to use its ability. This does not influence its behaviour towards initiating a hunt.
poltergeist.hunt: The Poltergeist will always throw an item every 0.5 seconds, instead of only having a 50% chance to do so.

raiju.name: Raiju
raiju.description: A Raiju is a demon that thrives on electrical current. While generally calm, they can become agitated when overwhelmed with power.
raiju.activity: When a Raiju manifests during a ghost event or a hunt, it will interfere with electronics that are up to 15 metres away on the same floor, instead of the usual 10 metres. This also applies to global chat.
raiju.hunt: When the Raiju is within {{distance}} meters of at least one piece of active electronic equipment on the same floor (that can also be located outside the investigation area), its hunt sanity threshold is increased to 65%, and it will move at a fixed speed during hunts. Otherwise, it will have the standard threshold of 50% and will follow standard ghost speeds with one particularity: if the Raiju has line-of-sight with a player while near active electronic equipment, the speed increase from continuous line-of-sight adds in the background, and will only be applied once it is no longer near any electronics. All effects listed above apply to most electronic equipment, whether they are placed, held in the hand, or dropped on the floor. The following do not count towards the speed boost or the hunt sanity threshold: - Global chat - Video cameras and Photo Cameras that are thrown on the ground - Motion sensors, sound sensors, and D.O.T.S. Projectors that are thrown on the ground or held (excluding T1 D.O.T.S., which also needs to be turned off) - Objects in the inventory (except flashlights that are turned on) - Any other electrical equipment not brought in from the truck (building lights, fuse box, CCTV, fans, etc.).
raiju.misc: The player's heartbeats can be heard within 15 metres of the Raiju, instead of within 10 metres like with other ghosts, making the heartbeats much louder with the Raiju compared to other ghosts. This is likely a bug.

revenant.name: Revenant
revenant.description: A Revenant is a violent ghost that will attack indiscriminately. Their speed can be deceiving, as they are slow while dormant; however, as soon as they hunt they can move incredibly fast.
revenant.hunt:
Revenants have very noticeable speed change between roaming and chasing modes. When a Revenant is roaming, it will move very slowly. However, as soon as it detects a player (either visually or through speech/electronics), it will begin to move extremely fast (nearly twice the base speed of most other ghosts) and sustains this speed until it reaches the spot where it last detected a player. If and when reverting to roaming mode, the Revenant's speed will slowly decrease over ~2.7 seconds back to its initial value.

Contrary to most other ghosts, the Revenant will not speed up with continuous line-of-sight.

shade.name: Shade
shade.description: A Shade is known to be very shy. There is evidence to suggest that a Shade will stop all paranormal activity if there are people nearby.
shade.activity:
On average, the Shade is less likely to perform interactions than other ghosts.

The Shade is less likely to perform ghost events at high sanity. At 100% average sanity, it has a 0% chance of successfully performing an event. This success rate increases by 2% per percentage of average sanity lost; at an average sanity of 50%, an attempted ghost event will always succeed.

When it performs a ghost event, the Shade has a higher chance of appearing as a shadow. If the ghost is made to appear using a Summoning Circle, a Music Box, or a Monkey Paw, it has a 50% chance of appearing as a black shadow rather than in its full form while in the ghost event stage. It will return to a fully visible form when the hunt begins.
shade.ability: If at least one person is in the same room as a Shade, it will be unable to perform interactions (including the fuse box and when players try to force an interaction through the Voodoo Doll), ghost events, or initiate hunts, regardless of average sanity. It may still perform these actions if it happens to wander into a room without players. Since interactions occur in a range, the Shade can still "reach" into the player's room from another room to interact with objects.
shade.hunt: The Shade can only hunt below an average sanity of 35%, lower than most other ghosts.

spirit.name: Spirit
spirit.description: Spirits are very common ghosts. They are very powerful, but passive, only attacking when they need to. They defend their place of death to the utmost degree, killing anyone that is caught overstaying their welcome.
spirit.activity: When Incense is used near a Spirit, it will not be able to initiate a hunt for 180 seconds instead of 90 seconds with most other ghosts. Like other ghosts, this will not prevent cursed hunts. This delay will also apply if the Spirit was smudged during a hunt.

thaye.name: Thaye
thaye.description: Thaye have been known to rapidly age over time, even in the afterlife. From what we've learned, they seem to deteriorate faster while within the presence of the living.
thaye.ability:
The Thaye has an internal "age" parameter that affects its general activity. The Thaye will attempt to age 1 minute after an exit door is opened for the first time; if at least one player is in the same room as the ghost or within 3 meters of it, the Thaye will add 1 to its age and re-attempt to age after 1-2 minutes, else it will re-attempt to age after 30 seconds. If the Thaye successfully uses this ability during a hunt, the age increase will only be effective after the hunt.

|Behaviour |	Age 0 (Initial) |	Per age added |	Age 10 and higher|
|---|---|---|---|
|Hunt sanity threshold|	75%|	-6%|	15%|
|Hunt speed|	2.75 m/s|	-0.175 m/s|	1 m/s|
|Relative interaction/ghost event rate|	200%|	-15%|	50%|

!> Detailed behaviour per age
|Age|	Hunt sanity threshold|	Relative activity rate|	Hunt speed|
|:---|---:|---:|---:|
|0|	75%|	200%|	2.75 m/s|
|1|	69%|	185%|	2.575 m/s|
|2|	63%|	170%|	2.4 m/s|
|3|	57%|	155%|	2.225 m/s|
|4|	51%|	140%|	2.05 m/s|
|5|	45%|	125%|	1.875 m/s|

For every age added, the Thaye's "human age" as provided by the Ouija Board increases by 1 - 4. Unlike ghost activity, there is no (reasonably attainable) limit on the Thaye's "human age". The Thaye's starting "human age" can still be anywhere from 10 - 90, like all other ghosts.

Once the Thaye has used its ability 9 times, it will no longer be able to perform ghost events unless forced through the use of cursed possessions.
thaye.hunt:
The Thaye hunting speed is determined by it's age.

It's hunt sanity threshold at age 0 is 75% and it will lose 6% per age added until it's age 10 and higher. Then the hunt sanity will be 15%.

Unlike most other ghosts, the Thaye does not speed up with line-of-sight of a player.

mimic.name: The Mimic
mimic.description: The Mimic is an elusive, mysterious, copycat ghost that mirrors traits and behaviours from others, including other ghost types.
mimic.ability:
The Mimic is able to imitate any type of ghost, and inherit all of its features and abilities:
- Interaction and ghost event rates and preferences
- Hunt thresholds
- Hunt movement speeds
- Various forms of special abilities (e.g. Poltergeist multi-throw, Demon ability hunt)

When imitating a type of ghost, The Mimic will not copy its types of evidence, and will not necessarily provide its guaranteed type of evidence on reduced-evidence difficulties such as Insanity, but can copy features related to evidence. For example, it is able to copy the Obake's six-fingered handprints or the Deogen's breathing, as The Mimic has Ultraviolet and Spirit Box as evidence, but it cannot copy the Goryo's trait of only appearing on a Video Camera when interacting with a D.O.T.S Projector, as The Mimic does not have D.O.T.S Projector as one of its types of evidence.

The Mimic will always start in the "blank" state (in which it essentially mimics itself) at the beginning of a contract. When this is the case, it will act as a default ghost and have no special abilities. It will attempt to change 1 minute after an exit door has been opened for the first time, then every 30 seconds to 2 minutes, but cannot change during hunts and ghost events.

The Mimic cannot imitate the Banshee or the Dayan if it is itself male (i.e. using a male ghost model, male vocalizations, and a male name).

The Mimic, when imitating some specific ghost types, will have some specific behaviours, listed below:
- If The Mimic imitates a Banshee, initially, it has no target. Once the first non-cursed hunt is attempted, a target is chosen randomly.
- If The Mimic imitates a Moroi, and curses the player through the Spirit Box, the Parabolic Microphone, or the Sound Recorder, the curse will remain even if The Mimic switches to another ghost type.
- If The Mimic imitates an Obambo, a random state will be selected.
- If The Mimic imitates a Thaye, a fixed age between 0 and 10 is randomly selected, and it will imitate another ghost using its own timer instead of the Thaye's ageing timer.

If The Mimic is affected by Incense, it will not be able to hunt for the duration associated with the ghost it was imitating at that moment, even if it imitates another ghost before its end.

The Mimic provides "evidence" of Ghost Orbs in addition to its three main evidence types, which also appear on difficulties with reduced evidence, including zero evidence. These Ghost Orbs, along with the other types of evidence if none are hidden due to the difficulty, will always exist regardless of the type of ghost that The Mimic chooses to imitate, and will behave in exactly the same way as those produced by other ghost types and will only levitate in the ghost room.

twins.name: The Twins
twins.description: These ghosts have been reported to mimic each other's actions. They alternate their attacks to confuse their prey.
twins.ability:
The Twins is simply one ghost. This means there is no "decoy twin" to:
- Set off motion sensors or step in salt
- Produce evidence of Freezing Temperatures (or even affect temperatures to begin with) or Spirit Box
- Perform ghost events or hunts at the same time

When The Twins tries to interact, one of the following occurs:
- 50% chance of performing one interaction within the normal range ({{distance}} metres).
- 30% chance of performing one interaction within a larger range (4 times the normal range).
- 20% chance of performing its ability, which produces two interactions, one in each range, in a timespan of 1 or 2 seconds.

All such interactions follow the standard 1/3 (33%) chance of producing EMF Level 5 instead of 2 or 3, regardless of which range was used to perform the interaction.
twins.hunt:
As The Twins is only one ghost, two hunts cannot occur simultaneously, and it will follow the standard 25-second cooldown between hunts.

When The Twins attempts to initiate a hunt, it will first perform a crucifix check at its current location before choosing to have a slow or a fast base speed, with each having a 50% chance. If choosing to be slow, the hunt will begin at its current location; if choosing to be fast, it will teleport close to the area where it last interacted with the large range and will hunt from there. Regardless of where The Twins hunts from, it will follow standard hunting rules.

If a cursed hunt is triggered, The Twins will always hunt from the current location, but it still has a 50% chance of selecting either base speed.

wraith.name: Wraith
wraith.description: Wraiths are one of the most dangerous ghosts you will find. It is also the only known ghost that has the ability of flight and has sometimes been known to travel through walls.
wraith.activity: The Wraith will never step in a salt pile, and therefore will never disturb them. This includes Tier III Salt during hunts, rendering it ineffective against one.
wraith.ability: When the Wraith is not hunting, it has a chance to teleport to a random player, generating an EMF Level 2 reading at the location where it teleported to, at the level of the targeted player's feet, with a 33% chance for this to be an EMF Level 5 reading instead. The Wraith will resume normal behaviour after teleporting.

yokai.name: Yokai
yokai.description: Yokai are common ghosts that are attracted to human voices. They can usually be found haunting family homes.
yokai.activity:
Utilizing voice chat near the Yokai at any sanity will increase its rate of activity.

When a Music Box event is triggered, the cursed hunt initiated from the ghost reaching the box triggers if the box is within 0.5 metres of the Yokai's head instead of 1 metre for all other ghosts. This means the cursed hunt will not instantly trigger if the Yokai reaches a crouching player holding the box.
yokai.hunt:
When at least one player uses voice chat in the same room as the Yokai, its hunt sanity threshold is temporarily increased to 80%. Otherwise, it has the standard threshold of 50%.

During hunts, a Yokai can only hear players or sense handheld active electronics that are within 2.5 metres of it. Its line-of-sight is unaffected.

yurei.name: Yurei
yurei.description: A Yurei is a ghost that has returned to the physical world, usually for the purpose of revenge or hatred.
yurei.activity:
When Incense is used on the Yurei, in addition to preventing hunts and temporarily increasing activity, it will return to its favourite room and be trapped within it for 90 seconds, stopping it from roaming through the location. It can still leave that room by performing a ghost event, but it will return to it once the event ends. If the Yurei is affected by incense during a hunt, it will only be trapped in its favourite room after the hunt ends for the remaining time of the cleansing effect.

Outside of its ability, the Yurei doesn't have an increased chance to interact with doors.

When interacting with a door, the Yurei cannot slightly move it and can only either close it completely, or open it completely. This doesn't apply to hunts.
yurei.ability:
When choosing to use its ability, the Yurei will first check if its current room has an opened door. Doors that count for this ability are mostly room doors, as well as exit doors, large tent doors on campsites, Dining Room cabinet doors and Living Room/Games Room fireplace doors on Point Hope, and washing machine doors and Morgue doors on Sunny Meadows. Hiding spot doors, however, do not count.

If the check is successful, the following is caused:
- All players within 7.5 metres of the ghost will have their sanity decreased by 15%. Players outside the investigation area will not be affected by the sanity drain.
- The ghost will randomly select one opened door in the room and close it fully in a smooth way (as opposed to a strong slam) without any creaking sound. This in turn produces an EMF 2 interaction on that door.
	- Large tent doors will not fully close.
